top_choice_rationale: P002 (Autor, Hanson, Katz) recognises a mature body of empirical work, running from the early 1990s into the 2010s. It asks one question: how technology and trade shift labour demand and who bears the adjustment. It answers with transparent designs that others have reanalysed and contested in the open. That standard of direct empirical confirmation is why I rank it above the more theory-driven alternatives. The citation should name the empirical contribution and not claim the whole task framework. That leaves the priority of Acemoglu, Levy and Murnane open. It should also state that Katz is credited for wage structure and education versus technology, not for the intergenerational-mobility work on B045. Costs remain: the three-name cap excludes Dorn, and the size and persistence of China-shock effects and shift-share identification are still debated. P001 (Melitz, Helpman) is a close second. It has a clear originating model and well-confirmed qualitative predictions, but it leaves out the empirical exporter-premium contributors and its welfare magnitudes depend on functional form. I rank both clearly above no award, because both are mature, scientifically substantial and attributable. I do not use the round-2 support counts (P001 has six explicit supporters, P002 has five) as evidence of merit.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile. I hold an adjunct appointment at Chicago Booth and am KVA Vice President, and I have a long committee overlap with Hassler and Krusell. My principal co-author Steven Kaplan is not credited on any proposal. The profile documents no co-authorship or institutional tie to Autor, Hanson, Katz, Melitz or Helpman. My field is corporate finance, so neither proposal is in my research area. Conflicts are disclosed, not adjudicated.
